title: SpeakNative
problem_statement: Approximately 1.5 billion people are learning English globally, and 73% of intermediate learners at the B1-B2 CEFR level stall for 12 or more months because dominant apps focus on vocabulary and grammar drills rather than spontaneous spoken conversation. Live human tutoring closes this gap functionally but costs $15-40 per session, limiting most learners to one or two sessions per week — far below the 10+ hours of conversation practice research shows is necessary to advance a CEFR level. The convergence of mature speech recognition, large language models capable of natural dialogue, and a 1.5-billion-person addressable market makes 2024 the right moment to deliver AI-powered daily conversation practice at an accessible price point. Without a scalable, affordable solution, hundreds of millions of learners will remain stuck at intermediate plateaus, limiting their professional mobility and social integration.
target_users: B1-B2 CEFR intermediate adult learner in a non-English-speaking country seeking career advancement in a multinational company
Recent immigrant to an English-speaking country needing conversational fluency for daily social and civic integration
University student preparing for an English-language academic program or international internship
Self-directed adult learner who has exhausted gamified vocabulary apps and wants structured speaking practice on a tight budget
user_stories: As a B1-B2 CEFR intermediate adult learner in a non-English-speaking country seeking career advancement in a multinational company, I want to complete a 10-minute AI-driven job interview simulation before my workday so that I can practice professional vocabulary and reduce hesitation in real meetings.

As a B1-B2 CEFR intermediate adult learner in a non-English-speaking country seeking career advancement in a multinational company, I want to receive immediate phoneme-level pronunciation feedback after each spoken turn so that I can identify and correct specific accent errors that undermine my credibility with native-speaking colleagues.

As a recent immigrant to an English-speaking country needing conversational fluency for daily social and civic integration, I want to role-play scenario conversations such as speaking with a landlord, visiting a clinic, or attending a parent-teacher meeting so that I can handle real-life interactions confidently without costly tutoring sessions.

As a recent immigrant to an English-speaking country needing conversational fluency for daily social and civic integration, I want the app to detect when I switch to my native language mid-sentence and gently prompt me to rephrase in English so that I build the habit of thinking and speaking in English rather than translating internally.

As a university student preparing for an English-language academic program or international internship, I want to practice timed spoken responses to IELTS Speaking or TOEFL Independent tasks with AI scoring so that I can track my band or score trajectory over time and know when I am ready for the real exam.

As a self-directed adult learner who has exhausted gamified vocabulary apps and wants structured speaking practice on a tight budget, I want unlimited daily AI conversation sessions for under $10 per month so that I can practice as often as research recommends without financial anxiety limiting my frequency.

As a self-directed adult learner who has exhausted gamified vocabulary apps and wants structured speaking practice on a tight budget, I want a weekly spoken fluency report showing words-per-minute, filler-word frequency, and grammatical error categories so that I can set concrete improvement goals without needing a human tutor to assess me.
acceptance_criteria: The AI conversation engine responds to a learner's spoken turn within 1.5 seconds of speech-end detection on a standard 4G mobile connection at least 95% of the time.
Speech recognition correctly transcribes B1-B2 learner speech with non-native accents at a Word Error Rate of 12% or lower across a benchmark set of 500 utterances spanning at least 10 accent groups.

After each conversation session, the app surfaces a structured feedback card identifying at least 3 grammatical error types, 3 mispronounced phonemes with audio model examples, and a fluency score on a 0-100 scale within 10 seconds of session end.

Role-play scenario library contains a minimum of 50 distinct real-life scenarios across 5 domains (workplace, social, healthcare, civic, academic) at launch, each with branching dialogue paths of at least 8 turns.
A learner's CEFR sub-level progress estimate, derived from spoken output analysis, updates after every completed session and is displayed with an explanation of the evidence used to generate it.

The app enforces English-only conversation mode by detecting native-language utterances with at least 90% precision and triggering an in-session English rephrasing prompt within one conversational turn.
Subscription checkout and first conversation session can be completed end-to-end in under 5 minutes on a first-time install on both iOS and Android.
All user audio data is encrypted in transit and at rest, retained for no more than 30 days by default, and fully deletable by the user via a single in-app action with confirmation within 24 hours.

success_metrics.metric: Weekly Active Speaking Minutes per paying subscriber
success_metrics.baseline: Estimated 20 minutes/week based on typical iTalki session frequency at comparable price points
Industry average for language-learning subscription apps: approximately 35%
success_metrics.target: 55% 30-day retention by end of Quarter 2 post-launch

success_metrics.metric: Percentage of active users who advance at least one CEFR sub-level within 90 days of consistent use (5+ sessions/week)
success_metrics.baseline: 0% (no prior product baseline; research benchmark: ~15% advance with 2 sessions/week of human tutoring)
success_metrics.target: 40% of qualifying users advance one CEFR sub-level within 90 days

success_metrics.metric: Net Promoter Score (NPS) among subscribers active for 30+ days
success_metrics.target: NPS of 50 or above by Month 6

success_metrics.metric: Average AI conversation turn latency (speech-end to AI audio response start)
success_metrics.baseline: Industry observed average for conversational AI voice apps: ~2.5 seconds
success_metrics.target: Below 1.5 seconds at p95 within 60 days of launch

risks_open_questions: Speech recognition accuracy degrades significantly for learners with strong regional accents (e.g., South Asian, West African, Southeast Asian English) — will WER targets be achievable across all accent groups without accent-specific model fine-tuning, and what is the cost and data availability to do so?

LLM-generated conversational responses may include factually incorrect information, culturally insensitive content, or inadvertently reinforce the learner's grammatical errors rather than correcting them — what guardrails, red-teaming, and human review processes are required pre-launch?

GDPR, CCPA, and emerging AI-specific data regulations require explicit consent for voice data storage; the legal basis for retaining audio to improve models must be established before launch — is a consent-based opt-in for model training data sufficient, or is a separate data processing agreement needed?

At a sub-$10/month price point, LLM inference and speech API costs per active user must remain below approximately $2/month to sustain margins — current per-session costs for GPT-4-class models and Whisper-class ASR may exceed this threshold at target usage levels; is model distillation or fine-tuned open-source models the right cost lever?

Open question: Should CEFR sub-level assessment be built on a validated psychometric framework (e.g., aligned to Cambridge or ALTE standards) requiring external validation studies, or is a proprietary proxy sufficient for product feedback purposes without regulatory risk?

Learner motivation and habit formation are the primary drivers of long-term retention; streaks and leaderboards are known to produce anxiety and churn in adult learners — what engagement mechanic best serves the demographic without replicating Duolingo's gamification criticisms?

The scenario role-play library requires culturally localized content for the top 10 learner markets (Brazil, India, Japan, Germany, France, etc.) — is AI-generated localization of scenario contexts sufficient, or does it require human cultural review to avoid misrepresenting norms and risking negative press?

Competitive risk: Duolingo has publicly announced an AI conversation product; Google and Microsoft have native speech AI capabilities — what is SpeakNative's defensible moat if large incumbents ship free conversation features within 12-18 months of our launch?
out_of_scope: Support for languages other than English as the target practice language at initial launch (e.g., AI-powered Spanish or Mandarin conversation practice)
Human tutor marketplace or live session booking functionality; SpeakNative is AI-only at launch with no human-in-the-loop tutoring component
Formal certification or official CEFR examination preparation with proctored testing and accredited score reporting
Reading, writing, or listening skill modules; the v1 product scope is spoken conversation practice only
B2B enterprise or school district licensing, LMS integrations, or bulk seat management dashboards
Offline mode or downloadable conversation packs for use without an internet connection
Content for absolute beginners at A1-A2 CEFR level; onboarding requires a minimum B1 placement score to enter the core conversation experience
Social or community features such as learner-to-learner conversation matching, forums, or leaderboards
